notes.claim: If the distribution can be assumed normal, an interval of plus or minus 2 standard deviations (k = 2) has a coverage probability of approximately 95 percent.
Some 99.7 percent of a normal population lies within 3 standard deviations of the mean, so a value beyond about 3.3 can be treated as an outlier.
An outlier should not be rejected automatically; ask why such a value occurred and answer that sensibly before considering rejection.
Extreme values distort the mean but not the median, so one odd reading moves the average more than the middle reading.
For data that follow a normal distribution, approximately 68% lie within one standard deviation of the mean, 95% within two and 99.7% within three.

sources.title: 1.3.5.1. Measures of Location
sources.quote: Extreme values in the tails distort the mean. However, these extreme values do not distort the median since the median is based on ranks.

sources.title: UKAS LAB 12: The Expression of Uncertainty in Testing
sources.quote: that the probability distribution can be assumed to be normal and that a value of k = 2 defines an interval having a coverage probability of approximately 95 %.

sources.title: HELM Workbook 36: Descriptive Statistics
sources.quote: Knowing that some 99.7% of a normal population lies within 3 standard deviations of the mean, we could treat any value further than say 3.3 standard deviations from the mean as on outlier.

sources.title: HELM Workbook 36: Descriptive Statistics
sources.quote: You should always ask why such a value occurred in the first place and work to answer such a question sensibly before considering rejection.

sources.title: 2.4: The Normal Distribution - Mathematics LibreTexts
sources.quote: Approximately 68% of the data is within one standard deviation of the mean. Approximately 95% of the data is within two standard deviations of the mean. Approximately 99.7% of the data is within three standard deviations of the mean.
